records.fullName: AMD Radeon RX Vega 64 Air Cooled
AMD Radeon RX Vega 64 Liquid Cooled

gaps: Dual-GPU desktop boards omitted (HD 7990 Malta, R9 295X2, Radeon Pro Duo): representing two GPUs as one GpuRecord would feed the fitted model a shader/TFLOPS figure no game can actually use, since CrossFire is dead in modern titles.

OEM-only rebadges omitted: Radeon R7 350 / R7 340 / R5 340X / R5 330 / R5 240, the entire RX 500X series (RX 550X/560X/570X/580X), RX 5300, OEM RX 5500 and RX 5600, RX 6300, RX 640/630. These were never sold at retail as standalone cards.
Pre-GCN VLIW parts sold under HD 7000 marketing names (HD 7670, HD 7570, HD 7510, HD 7450) omitted: they are TeraScale rebrands, outside the GCN 1.0+ remit.

China/regional SKUs omitted for lack of confident clocks: RX 6750 GRE 12GB and 10GB, RX 7650 GRE, RX 580 2048SP, RX 470D, RX 560D, and the non-XT RX 9060. Each is a real product; I could not recall boost clocks to within the 8% fp32 consistency band and would not guess.
RX 5700 XT 50th Anniversary Edition omitted: identical silicon to the RX 5700 XT with a 75 MHz higher boost, low value against the risk of family-ordering noise.

lengthMm and slotWidth are null on every record: both are AIB-board properties, not chip properties, and vary by 100mm+ across partners for the same SKU. The harvest pipeline should source these per board, not per SKU.
pciIds omitted entirely: pci-ids.ucw.cz and TechPowerUp are egress-blocked, and PCI device IDs are exactly the class of datum where a near-miss from memory is worse than absence.

driverEolDate is null on all records including the eol GCN 1.0-3.0 parts: I am confident about the status (AMD moved GCN 1.0-3.0 to legacy driver branches) but not about the precise announcement/final-driver dates.
Mobile and Radeon Pro / FirePro / Instinct parts excluded per remit.
uncertainties: boostClockMHz is AMD's boost (peak) clock throughout, never the 'game clock'. For RDNA 1-4 AMD's marketing leads with game clock; using it would have understated fp32 by 8-20% and broken the shaders*clock*2 consistency rule against AMD's own published TFLOPS.

fp32TFLOPS for RDNA 3 and RDNA 4 is the single-issue figure (shaders*boost*2). AMD markets double these numbers (61.4 TFLOPS for the RX 7900 XTX, 48.7 for the RX 9070 XT) by counting dual-issue FP32, which only applies to co-issuable instruction pairs. The validator formula demands single-issue, and single-issue is the better predictor of game raster throughput; consumers of this data must not compare these figures with AMD's marketing slides.

Infinity Cache has no field on GpuRecord, so effective bandwidth is understated for RDNA 2-4. Sizes: RX 6950/6900/6800 XT/6800 128MB; 6750 XT/6700 XT 96MB; 6700 80MB; 6650 XT/6600 XT/6600 32MB; 6500 XT/6400 16MB; 7900 XTX 96MB; 7900 XT 80MB; 7900 GRE/7800 XT 64MB; 7700 XT 48MB; 7600 XT/7600 32MB; 9070 XT/9070 64MB; 9060 XT 32MB.

RX 5600 XT is recorded at its post-launch BIOS (1750 MHz boost, 14 Gbps memory, 336 GB/s). Launch-BIOS cards shipped at 1560 MHz boost and 12 Gbps (288 GB/s) and many were never reflashed; a single record cannot express both.
RX 9070 GRE has null base/boost clock and therefore null fp32TFLOPS. Shader count (3072), 12GB on a 192-bit bus and the 220W TBP I am confident about; the clocks I am not.
R9 290X and R9 290 tdpW (290W / 275W) are the widely-cited board figures; AMD never published a TDP for Hawaii. HD 7970 GHz Edition is 250W typical with a ~300W board maximum.
powerConnectors reflects the AMD reference board. Partner cards routinely add a connector (RX 570/580 8-pin+6-pin, RX 460/560 with a 6-pin, R7 250X variants). Treat as a floor, not a fixed fact.
recommendedPsuW is AMD's system-level recommendation where I am confident of it and null otherwise; it is a marketing guideline, not a measurement.

caps.vulkanVersion is a conservative floor per architecture (1.2 for GCN 1.0-3.0, 1.3 for GCN 4.0 onward). Actual exposed version depends on the installed driver branch; current Adrenalin exposes 1.4 on RDNA 2+.
caps.resizableBar is true from RDNA 1 onward because AMD backported Smart Access Memory to the RX 5000 series by driver in 2021; it is false for Polaris and Vega, which never got official support.

caps.upscaling is empty for GCN 1.0-3.0 and ['fsr'] from Polaris onward, matching AMD's official FSR support list. FSR 1 is a spatial post-process and does in practice run on HD 7000/R200/R300 hardware, so the empty list understates what those cards can do in FSR1-only titles.

shaderModel/dxFeatureLevel follow silicon, not marketing series: R7 370 and R9 270/270X/280/280X are Pitcairn/Tahiti (GCN 1.0, FL 11_1) while the R9 285/380/380X are Tonga (GCN 3.0, FL 12_0) and R9 390/390X are Hawaii (GCN 2.0, FL 12_0). The 200/300 series therefore splits across three feature levels.

Genuine naming inversion retained: R9 285 (1792 SP, Tonga) has fewer shaders than R9 280X (2048 SP, Tahiti) despite the higher model number. This is real AMD 200-series behaviour, not a data error; a family-monotonicity check that sorts by model number will flag it.
RX 6500 XT 8GB is a board-partner-only configuration (Sapphire, ASRock) rather than an AMD-reference SKU; it is emitted because the 4GB/8GB split materially changes VRAM gating.
RX 6700 10GB launchDate is null: the part is real (Navi 22 XL, 2304 SP, 160-bit, 175W) but its rollout was staggered and partly regional, and I do not trust my recollection of a date.

RX 7600 boostClockMHz is 2655, which is the figure I recall from AMD's spec page; AMD's own 21.5 TFLOPS (dual-issue) headline back-solves to 2625 MHz instead. The 1.1% discrepancy does not threaten the consistency band (fp32 here is computed from the stated clock) but the harvester should settle it.

HD 7730 memory configuration (1GB GDDR5, 128-bit, 4.5 Gbps) is my least-confident memory spec in the file, and its die attribution (Cape Verde LE vs Oland XT, both 384 SP) is likewise shaky; DDR3 versions of this part also existed.
Radeon RX Vega 64 carries variant 'Air Cooled' purely to disambiguate it from the Liquid Cooled Edition record; AMD's retail name for it is just 'Radeon RX Vega 64'.
R7 240 is recorded as the 2GB DDR3 128-bit configuration at 780 MHz; GDDR5 and 1GB versions also shipped and are not separately represented.
R9 270X/R9 270/R7 265 chip names are given as Curacao (the 300-series-era name for the Pitcairn respin); some sources label these Pitcairn XT/Pro. Architecture (GCN 1.0) is unaffected.
RX 9060 XT pcieLanes is set to 16 (Navi 44 is PCIe 5.0 x16, unlike the x8 RX 7600 it replaces); this is the RDNA 4 spec point I would most want re-checked by the harvester.
